title: Balancing Redox Reactions
notes: **Oxidation number method:** (1) write unbalanced equation, (2) assign oxidation numbers, (3) identify atoms oxidized and reduced, (4) equalize electron loss and gain by multiplying half-reactions, (5) combine and balance O and H using $H_2O$ and $H^+$ (acidic) or $OH^-$ (basic).
**Ion-electron (half-reaction) method:** split into oxidation half-reaction and reduction half-reaction. Balance each for atoms and charge, then combine so electrons cancel.
**Acidic medium:** balance O with $H_2O$, balance H with $H^+$, balance charge with electrons.
**Basic medium:** balance as in acid, then add $OH^-$ to both sides to neutralize $H^+$, forming $H_2O$.

**Example:** $MnO_4^- + Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + Fe^{3+}$ in acid: $MnO_4^- + 5e^- + 8H^+ \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O$ and $Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{3+} + e^-$. Combined: $MnO_4^- + 5Fe^{2+} + 8H^+ \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 5Fe^{3+} + 4H_2O$.
